title: Count Valid Word Occurrences
summary: Given an array of strings chunks, concatenate them to form a string s.
statement: Given an array of strings chunks, concatenate them to form a string s. An array of strings queries is also provided. A joiner hyphen is a hyphen in s with both preceding and following characters being lowercase letters. A word is a maximal substring of s consisting only of lowercase letters and joiner hyphens, with other characters acting as separators. Return an array ans where each element ans[i] represents the count of occurrences of queries[i] as a word in s.
constraints: A hyphen belongs to a word only when both adjacent original characters are lowercase letters; lowercase letters and joiner hyphens form maximal words.
Every other character separates words; return occurrence counts for each query.
hints: Chunk boundaries disappear before lexical analysis.
Scan the joined text, treating lowercase letters and only two-sided letter hyphens as word characters.
Flush the current maximal token at every other character and count tokens.
Local neighbor checks exactly identify joiner hyphens, while flushing produces maximal words without overlap.
editorial: Local neighbor checks exactly identify joiner hyphens, while flushing produces maximal words without overlap.

tests.explanation: Concatenation forms words hello, world, hello, producing [2,1,0].
The chunk boundary does not matter: the hyphen lies between lowercase letters, so a-b occurs once.
